paragraph: The single-family market in Carlstadt is thin, with three sales over six months at a median of $640,000 and nothing selling above asking. The sale-to-list ratio of 0.99 and a median of 32 days on market say sellers are okay with waiting for the right buyer rather than pricing to move fast, but three sales is too small a sample to build a case on. Multi-family is where the actual volume sits, ten sales at a median of $770,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.05, and 60 percent of them closing above list in a median of about 26 days. That is competitive without being frenzied. The range runs from $640,000 up to $1,425,000, so treat the median as your guide rather than the extremes. Buying a two or three family here usually means inheriting tenants, leases, and a different financing conversation than a single-family purchase, which not every buyer is aware of going in. The monthly data is too sparse to call a seasonal direction; if Carlstadt follows the usual Bergen arc, expect closings to taper through the fall. If you're weighing the two, the deciding factor is whether you want a house to yourself or rental income attached to it.
